free_tier.stated: 20 GB per record, 10 GB per file, and explicitly unlimited records and unlimited files.

egress.terms: Free, unmetered, direct per-file content URLs (GET /api/records/<id>/files/<name>/content). No egress terms or pricing exist; EUDAT is publicly funded.

tooling: InvenioRDM-style REST API (live: GET /api/records?size=1 -> 200 with hits/entries and per-file content links); OAI-PMH; DOI minting (10.23728). Python client via plain requests. No rclone backend.
chaining: 20 GB per record x unlimited records. 50 records = 1 TB; 1,000 records = 20 TB in one account. The docs state outright 'There is no limit to the number of files you can deposit or records you can create'.
limits_note: 10 GB per file, 20 GB per record — so 20 TB needs ~1,024 records, which trips EUDAT's 'fair share' clause: 'the uploading of large number of files or creating large number of records is not considered fair use' and they ask you to contact them first. Live rate limit header: x-ratelimit-limit: 500, x-ratelimit-remaining: 499.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Rate-limited at 500 requests/window and watched for bulk growth; EUDAT says it 'will increase back-end storage capacity incrementally when necessary', which implies throttling rather than deletion, but the fair-share clause is the trigger for manual review.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: 'the maximum size for a record is 20 GB; and the maximum size for a file is 10 GB'
'There is no limit to the number of files you can deposit or records you can create'; 'fair share' principle
